relations.myth: Raphael pursues and binds Asmodeus in Egypt
relations.note: Raphael enables the fish fumigation, pursues Asmodeus to Egypt, and binds him.

relations.myth: God sends Raphael to heal Sarah
relations.note: God hears the prayers and sends Raphael, whose intervention defeats Asmodeus.

relations.myth: Asmodeus names Raphael as his frustrator
relations.note: Asmodeus identifies Raphael and fish smoke as powers that frustrate and repel him.
Ashmedai reports that the Prince of the Sea entrusted the shamir to a bird.
Medieval Jewish demonology names Naamah as Ashmedai's mother.
Medieval Jewish demonology names the angel or demon Shamdon as Ashmedai's father.
A competing later Jewish genealogy names Agrat bat Mahlat as Ashmedai's mother.
A variant later tradition presents Agrat bat Mahlat as Ashmedai's sexual partner.
Kabbalistic demonology pairs Asmodeus with the younger Lilith as his consort.
Some kabbalistic schemes place Asmodeus beneath or alongside Samael's demonic royal pair.
Some kabbalistic schemes place Asmodeus beneath or alongside the elder Lilith's royal pair.
Modern scholarship proposes Aēšma as Asmodeus's linguistic-religious antecedent, with conceptual continuity remaining uncertain.
Comparative tradition equates Ashmedai with Ṣakhr because both steal Solomon's ring and usurp his throne.
